location.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
location.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
location.notes: Represents recruitment university sites, not individual participant residence.

subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers provided in main text; may exist in Table S1 (not included).

sample_id.notes: No individual sample identifiers provided in the main text.

subcohort.value: Central Africa (n=17) and Indian peninsula (n=18) travel groups
subcohort.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
subcohort.notes: Two travel-destination subcohorts reported; not stratified per-field in most demographic data.

control.notes: Study design is a before/after travel cohort, not case-control.

country.evidence_quote: 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs
country.notes: Fecal specimens were collected in Sweden before and after travel.

body_site.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs

days_from_first_collection.notes: Paper reports median days before departure (4) and after return (22) but not a single days-from-first-collection value.

westernized.evidence_quote: 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs on the Indian peninsula or in Central Africa
westernized.notes: Inferred from Swedish nationality/residence; not explicitly labeled 'westernized' in text.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Sequence data have been submitted to the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB7369.

age.notes: Reported as a range (23-34), not a single age value; see age_min/age_max.

sex.notes: Reported as aggregate cohort proportion (74% female, 26/35), not a per-participant categorical value; granularity is study-level.

age_years.notes: Only a range (23-34 years) reported, no mean/median age value given.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Applies to both before and after travel sampling; also reiterated: 'the increase observed occurred without any antibiotic intake.'

disease.notes: No disease/condition reported for study participants (healthy students undergoing exchange programs); default 'Healthy' applied per schema guidance, not explicitly stated in text.

disease_details.notes: Study subjects were healthy Swedish students; no disease condition described, but 'Healthy' status not explicitly stated in text.

disease_response_orr.notes: No treatment response/oncology context in this paper.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable; study is not oncology-related.

disease_response_recist.notes: Not applicable; no tumor response criteria used.

feces_phenotype.notes: Fecal specimens were analyzed for microbiome/resistance genes but no specific stool phenotype (e.g., consistency, occult blood) reported.

fmt_id.notes: No fecal microbiota transplantation performed in this study.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Adult study population; no neonatal data.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Not reported; subjects were 23-34 years old, unlikely menopausal but not stated.

treatment.evidence_quote: All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
treatment.notes: Specific agents mentioned in Discussion include mefloquine, proguanil, and atovaquone, but not all subjects used same agent; antibiotics were explicitly excluded ('None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling').

biomarker_name.notes: Paper reports resistance gene abundances and taxonomic changes rather than clinical biomarkers matching this schema's intent; not extracted to avoid mismatched interpretation.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; paper concerns gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance, no tumor data.

uncurated_metadata.notes: No additional free-text metadata identified beyond schema fields.

study_name.notes: No canonical study name (e.g., 'AuthorX_Year') is provided in the text; only ENA accession PRJEB7369 is given.

curator.notes: Curator information not applicable to paper content.

pmid.notes: PMID taken from paper_id field provided in input metadata, not from body text.

target_condition.evidence_quote: we used explorative shotgun metagenomic sequencing to address the abundance of >300 antibiotic resistance genes
target_condition.notes: Study focuses on antibiotic resistance gene abundance and acquisition of ESBL-producing E. coli after international travel.

dna_extraction_kit.notes: The paper states 'DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens' but does not name a specific kit or protocol in the provided text.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000 technology.
sequencing_platform.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
sequencing_platform.notes: Isolate genomes (ESBL-positive) were separately sequenced on Illumina MiSeq (250-bp paired-end reads); main metagenomic sequencing used HiSeq 2000.

extraction_warnings: Individual-level demographic and sample data (subject_id, sample_id, exact age, sex per person) are likely provided only in Supplementary Table S1, which was not included in the provided text; these fields could not be extracted at sample_level.
Age is reported only as a cohort range (23-34 years), not as mean/median or per-subject values.
Sex is reported only as an aggregate percentage (74% female, 26/35), not per-subject.

Two travel-destination subcohorts (Central Africa n=17, Indian peninsula n=18) exist but most extracted schema fields are reported only at whole-cohort (study) level rather than stratified by subcohort in the main text.
'disease' field value 'Healthy' is an inferred default per schema instructions since no disease/condition was explicitly reported for participants; confidence is low.

This paper concerns healthy Swedish students traveling abroad and gut microbiome/antibiotic resistance gene analysis; most schema fields (oncology, neonatal, obgyn, HLA, ECOG, biomarkers as defined) are not applicable to this study's content.

The 'treatment' field was populated with antimalarial chemoprophylaxis use, which may not align with the schema's intended clinical treatment context (e.g., NCIT:C1908 medication); reviewer should verify appropriateness.

Disease status of participants (healthy) is implied by study design (health care students traveling, exclusion of antibiotic use) but never explicitly stated as 'Healthy' in the text, so left as not_reported per no-fabrication rule.

No subgroup-level schema fields were populated despite the paper containing subgroup data (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula) because none of the schema's required fields matched paper content at subgroup level.
study_name field could not be derived from any explicit canonical identifier in the text; only ENA accession PRJEB7369 was found.
dna_extraction_kit not explicitly named in the provided text; only general statement 'DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens' given.
pmid value was taken from the paper_id metadata field rather than from within the paper text itself.
